metadata.site: Boxwork unit, Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), Gale Crater, Mars. 4 km study area centered 4.808 S, 137.372 E.
metadata.selectionNote: Targets 1-3 are placed at Curiosity's real end-of-drive position on the sol it worked there (NASA/JPL MMGIS waypoints). Target 4 is the rover's latest reported position. Target 5 is our own selection from HiRISE 1 m terrain: a ridge field the rover did not visit.
metadata.coordinateSystem: Planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude (IAU Mars 2015 sphere)

properties.name: Altadena Drill Site
properties.kind: Drilled bedrock at the edge of the boxwork
properties.why: Curiosity's first drill sample in the boxwork region (June 2025). Bedrock here differs in composition from other Mount Sharp layers.
properties.detail: On sol 4571 Curiosity stood here and drilled the rock nicknamed "Altadena". JPL reports that the bedrock between the boxwork ridges has a different composition from other Mount Sharp layers and contains calcium sulfate veins, which had not been seen in this sulfate-rich layer before. A human geologist could sample many veins quickly and compare fresh and weathered surfaces.
properties.findings: Look for: pale calcium-sulfate veins cutting darker bedrock; the drill hole itself (about 1.6 cm wide); fractured slabs and loose angular rocks (see photo).
properties.source: NASA/JPL news, "NASA's Curiosity Mars Rover Starts Unpacking Boxwork Formations" (June 2025); rover position: MMGIS waypoint, sol 4571
properties.selectionNote: Real rover position on the drill sol (NASA/JPL MMGIS)

properties.name: Monte Grande Hollow & Nevado Sajama Ridge
properties.kind: Boxwork ridge and hollow, both drilled
properties.why: The key boxwork test: Curiosity drilled a hollow (Valle de la Luna) and the ridge beside it (Nevado Sajama), about 10 m apart and 2 m different in height.
properties.detail: Boxwork ridges are thought to be fractures that groundwater filled with mineral cement; wind then eroded the softer rock around them. Comparing ridge and hollow chemistry tests that idea. Curiosity needed several weeks (sols ~4695-4718) to find drillable bedrock in a sand-covered hollow. An astronaut with a shovel and a hand lens could do the same comparison in an afternoon.
properties.findings: Look for: cemented ridge blocks standing above sand-floored hollows; fractures and vein fill along ridge crests; whether ridge rock is harder or lighter-toned than hollow rock.
properties.source: NASA Curiosity blog, Sols 4709-4715 "Drilling high and low in the boxwork unit" and Sols 4716-4722 "Drilling success at Nevado Sajama" (Nov 2025); Siebach & Grotzinger (2014), JGR Planets 119, doi:10.1002/2013JE004508
properties.selectionNote: Real rover position during the ridge drill campaign (NASA/JPL MMGIS)

properties.name: Boxwork Entry Overlook
properties.kind: First close-up of the boxwork ridges
properties.why: Where Curiosity first saw the boxwork up close (May 2025). Good survey point to choose which ridges to sample.
properties.detail: Around sol 4548 the rover took a 291-image mosaic of crisscrossing low ridges, some only a few centimetres tall. These ridges had only been seen from orbit before. JPL notes that boxwork patterns have not been spotted anywhere else on the mountain, so this is a one-of-a-kind field site.
properties.findings: Look for: low curb-like ridges crossing in a box pattern; fractured bedrock; loose rocks that could trip a suited walker.
properties.source: NASA/JPL news (June 2025); rover position: MMGIS waypoint, sol 4548
properties.selectionNote: Real rover position on the survey sol (NASA/JPL MMGIS)

properties.name: Rendezvous with Curiosity
properties.why: Meet the rover: inspect wheel wear, clean dust from instruments, or hand-pick the next drill target together. Humans and robots working as one team.
properties.detail: This is the most recent end-of-drive position NASA/JPL has published for Curiosity (sol 5073, about 38.6 km driven since landing). Its weather (REMS) and radiation (RAD) sensors measure the conditions used in this planner. The marker updates whenever the data script is re-run.
properties.findings: Look for: bright bedrock plates and dark sand ripples (see photo); the rover's wheel tracks; buttes of upper Mount Sharp on the horizon.

properties.name: Uncharted Ridge Field
properties.kind: New science: boxwork ridges no rover has visited
properties.why: A polygonal ridge network, like the one Curiosity drilled at Monte Grande, that no rover has visited. About 0.8 km west of Curiosity's path and only ~450 m from base.
properties.detail: We spotted this field in the HiRISE 25 cm image: the same box-shaped ridge pattern as at Monte Grande. Curiosity's route passed to the east. If these ridges have the same cement as the drilled ones, the ancient groundwater system was wider than the rover has shown. An astronaut can map and sample it in one short EVA.
properties.findings: Look for: ridge spacing and height compared with Monte Grande; vein colour on ridge crests; sand-filled hollows. Collect hand samples from 3 ridges and 1 hollow.
properties.source: Our selection from HiRISE image ESP_019988_1750 (0.25 m/px) and DTM DTEEC_019698_1750_019988_1750_U01; not visited by Curiosity
